solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: In South America, you shouldn’t have time for snob’s preoccupation

indicators.note: saying one thing is in another asks for it to sit inside, surrounded on both sides

blocks.note: S is the compass abbreviation for south
a polite response to a gift, as is ta, British slang for thanks
T is the standard abbreviation for time
the United States, a common short form

explanation.surface: A traveller in South America is told there is no time for social climbing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South America' looks like one place, but it is S and US bracketing TA and T. Ta is everyday British for 'thank you', which 'you shouldn't have' also says.
explanation.definitionFit: Snobs care above all about social standing and rank, which is what this word means.

clue.text: The writer behind article showing feature of some crosswords

indicators.note: one thing coming behind another means it follows it in the written order

blocks.note: the definite article
the setter refers to themself as 'the writer', so ME

explanation.surface: An author stands behind a newspaper article about crosswords.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The writer' is a crossword convention for the setter, giving ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Some puzzles are built around a unifying topic that links several entries in the grid.

clue.text: Perhaps avoid firing Charlie during merger

indicators.note: something happening during another event falls within its span, so one piece sits inside

blocks.note: a takeover joins two companies
Charlie is C in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A company lets someone called Charlie go in the middle of a merger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firing' reads as sacking an employee, but in the definition it means gunfire; 'Perhaps' warns that dodging bullets is just one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers under gunfire duck behind shelter to stay out of harm's way, an example of this phrase.

clue.text: Kind to give away one shilling in coins

indicators.note: giving something away means you no longer have it, so a letter goes

blocks.note: a kind or sort
s is the old abbreviation for a shilling, a pre-decimal British coin

explanation.surface: A generous person hands over a shilling in loose change.
explanation.walkthrough: Only one of the two S letters goes, the final one.
explanation.definitionFit: Specie is money in metal form, as opposed to paper notes, so it means hard cash in coins.

clue.text: Good effort to limit publicity, say, about smartphones etc

indicators.note: a limit is a boundary, so these letters form the edges with the rest between
turned about means facing the opposite way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: G is the usual abbreviation for good
an advertisement
e.g., for example
an attempt

explanation.surface: A decent attempt to keep a lid on hype around smartphones and similar devices.
explanation.walkthrough: G and TRY together are the outer edges, holding AD plus the reversed EG.
explanation.definitionFit: Smartphones and similar electronic devices are collectively clever gizmos, the definition being a group of examples.

clue.text: Soldier on charge probed by a court dealing with minor complaints

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the noun: what this kind of medicine does

indicators.note: a probe goes into something, so the probing letters are placed inside

blocks.note: a senior army officer
the charge for something
taken as written
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A soldier facing a charge is questioned by a court that handles petty matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On charge' and 'court' suggest a military trial, and 'complaints' sounds legal; here complaints are ailments. General practice is family medicine, where GPs see everyday illnesses.
explanation.definitionFit: Family doctors, known as GPs in Britain, treat everyday ailments before referring serious cases to specialists.

clue.text: Offer a cartoonish view of revolutionary female desires to stop housework?

indicators.note: a revolution turns things round, so these letters run the other way
stopping a gap means plugging it, so these letters fill the middle

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for female
a yen is a longing
do-it-yourself, work done on one's own home

explanation.surface: A radical woman's wish to avoid doing chores is pictured as a cartoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary female' suggests a feminist, but the word reverses F and YENS together; the question mark admits DIY is only loosely housework.
explanation.definitionFit: Walt Disney's studio made animated films that sweeten and simplify stories, and the verb means to treat something that way.

clue.text: Cite Rocky boxing face of heavyweight Creed

indicators.note: the face is the front, so only the opening letter is wanted
rocky means shaky and unstable, so the letters are knocked out of order
to box something is to enclose it, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the first letter of heavyweight

explanation.surface: Rocky Balboa and Apollo Creed, the heavyweight boxers of the Rocky films.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all about the boxing films: Rocky and Creed are both characters, yet here one scrambles letters and the other is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethic is a set of moral principles a person lives by, much as a creed is a set of beliefs.

clue.text: Drinks consumed, hosting European Parliament’s supporter

indicators.note: a host has guests inside, so this word holds another piece

blocks.note: a round of drinks bought for a group
had, as in ate or drank
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Drinks are downed at a party for a backer of the European Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European Parliament' looks like one unit, but it splits: European gives E, and Parliament belongs to the definition. Roundheads fought for Parliament against the King in the English Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: In the English Civil War, followers of Parliament were nicknamed for their short-cropped hair.

clue.text: Figure in Dickens novel shows game played on board

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, surrounded
novel means new, so the letters take a new form

blocks.note: a number
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A character in a novel by Dickens plays a game on board ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure in Dickens novel' suggests a character, but figure is a number and novel scrambles the author's name around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Deck tennis is a ring-tossing game played over a net on passenger ships, so 'on board' is literal.

clue.text: Yank from westerly Honolulu, a Hawaiian

indicators.note: taking letters from a phrase means lifting them straight out of it
heading west in an across entry means going right to left, backwards

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the city name into the next words

explanation.surface: An American from Honolulu is described as a Hawaiian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yank' looks like a noun for an American, fitting Honolulu, but it is the verb meaning pull.
explanation.definitionFit: To yank is to pull hard, and to haul is to drag or tug something with force.

clue.text: Spice Girl greeting old king and wise man

blocks.note: Mel C, Sporty Spice of the 1990s pop group
an informal hello
O is the abbreviation for old
R, from Latin rex

explanation.surface: A pop star greets an aged monarch and a sage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old king' tempts as one unit such as a historic ruler, but it is O and R. Mel C was Sporty Spice in the Spice Girls.
explanation.definitionFit: By tradition, Melchior was one of the three Magi who brought gifts to the infant Jesus.

clue.text: Once working detective’s case, turn to Morse?

indicators.note: working means being processed or operated on, so the letters are reshaped
a case is the outside shell, so only the outer letters are kept

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the first and last letters of detective

explanation.surface: A former detective takes a case and calls in Inspector Morse.
explanation.walkthrough: Morse is the TV detective, which 'detective' and 'case' support; in the definition it is Morse code.
explanation.definitionFit: Converting a message into Morse code means turning plain text into a system of signals.

clue.text: Coerced worker saving energy, possibly a Pole

indicators.note: saving in the old sense of except means leaving something out

blocks.note: someone forced to work
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A forced labourer conserving energy may be from Poland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saving' reads as keeping energy, but in the older sense of 'except' it removes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Poles belong to the wider Slavic peoples of Eastern Europe, so a Pole is one example.

clue.text: Perhaps Santa has a place aboard space vehicle

indicators.note: passengers aboard are inside the vessel, so these letters go within

blocks.note: taken as written
PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names
a craft that touches down on a planet or moon

explanation.surface: Father Christmas gets a seat on a spacecraft instead of his sleigh.
explanation.walkthrough: Santa's traditional home is often said to be Lapland, in the far north of Finland, hence 'Perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: Popular legend places Father Christmas in Arctic Lapland, making him a resident of that region.

clue.text: Con keeping tabs on parliament’s leader for David Cameron, say

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside, so these letters are enclosed
a leader goes at the front, so only the opening letter is wanted

blocks.note: a convict serving a life sentence
the opening letter of parliament
tabs of ecstasy, each E in drug slang

explanation.surface: A convict keeps watch on the head of Parliament on behalf of the former prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeping tabs on' looks like one idiom for watching; it splits into the container signal, E for ecstasy doubled, and 'on' placing them after P. Cameron sits in the House of Lords for life.
explanation.definitionFit: The ex-premier was given a seat in the House of Lords that cannot be inherited, one example of such a title.

clue.text: Puritans holding rhubarb sticks out

indicators.note: to hold something is to grip it inside, so one piece is enclosed

blocks.note: prim, easily shocked people
rhubarb is British slang for nonsense

explanation.surface: Strict puritans holding rhubarb stalks that poke out.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhubarb here is nonsense, not the plant; both mean rubbish talk in British English.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that sticks out extends beyond the surface around it, which is what the verb describes.

clue.text: Band held up by a person who loses their kit

indicators.note: in a down entry, being held up by something means sitting on top of it

blocks.note: a narrow strip or band
as in 'ten pounds a day', meaning each

explanation.surface: A music band is delayed by a musician who has lost their equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' and 'kit' suggest a group and its drum kit; kit is British for clothes. 'A' as PER is the sense in 'twice a week'.
explanation.definitionFit: An exotic dancer takes off their clothing piece by piece as a performance.

clue.text: Musical work closed with finale from tenor, which may be a plus

indicators.note: the finale is the closing part, so only the last letter is kept

blocks.note: a staged musical drama
as in 'push the door to'
the final letter of tenor

explanation.surface: An opera that ends with the tenor's big number may be a bonus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plus' looks like a bonus, but it is the mathematical sign. 'To' meaning shut, as in a door pushed to, is a British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics, symbols for addition or multiplication are the signs that act on numbers.

clue.text: Quaint version of ancient, gold-embellished cups

indicators.note: to cup is to hold something within the hands, so the letters lie inside

blocks.note: the letters span the join in the hyphenated word

explanation.surface: A charming antique style of gilded drinking cups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cups' reads as the nouns being described, but it is a verb holding the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The fake-archaic spelling of old, as in 'ye olde tea shoppe', is used for mock-historic charm.

clue.text: Fit in extensive jacket of brocade, at first

indicators.note: a jacket covers the outside, so only the outer letters are kept
coming first means placed at the start of the answer

blocks.note: the first and last letters of brocade
lengthy

explanation.surface: A long brocade jacket that is a good fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At first' moves BE to the front, ahead of the word given before it.
explanation.definitionFit: To fit in is to feel at home and accepted as part of a group or place.

clue.text: Aggressive kind of personality picked up Asian capital

indicators.note: picking up a signal means catching its sound, so what is heard matters

blocks.note: Type A describes a driven, competitive temperament

explanation.surface: Someone with a pushy temperament has been noticed in an Asian city.
explanation.walkthrough: Type A is the psychology label for tense, ambitious, competitive people, as against laid-back Type B.
explanation.definitionFit: Taipei is the seat of government of Taiwan, its largest city.

clue.text: Scrubbing hard, burnish copper from Ireland

indicators.note: to scrub a plan is to cancel it, so a letter is struck out

blocks.note: to rub until shiny
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Scouring and polishing a piece of Irish copper metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrubbing' and 'burnish' paint metal cleaning and 'copper' the metal; here copper is slang for a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: In Irish and Scottish speech this word means the police, or a single police officer.

clue.text: Specific about Shakespeare part getting bowdlerised

blocks.note: c. for circa, about
King Lear, a title role
censored by removing passages

explanation.surface: Being precise about a Shakespeare role that has been censored.
explanation.walkthrough: Bowdler published a Shakespeare with the rude bits removed, which is why bowdlerised means censored.
explanation.definitionFit: Something clear-cut is sharply defined and unambiguous, as a specific detail is.

clue.text: Times contributors are getting on in employment

blocks.note: the people who write for this newspaper, speaking of themselves
to age is to grow older

explanation.surface: Older writers for the newspaper are still in work.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is set in The Times, so its contributors can call themselves 'us'.
explanation.definitionFit: Employment in the sense of putting something to use, as in 'the employment of force'.

clue.text: Legend in swimming area, cycling around

indicators.note: going round in a cycle moves the front letter to the back

blocks.note: a lido is an open-air public swimming pool

explanation.surface: A sporting hero is spotted in the pool doing laps.
explanation.walkthrough: A lido is a public outdoor pool, common in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend is a celebrated figure who is admired and hero-worshipped by fans.

clue.text: Oscar tucked into proper lard I cooked in a kind of soup

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective, the kind of soup rather than the soup

indicators.note: tucking one thing into others mixes it in among them before the shuffle
cooking transforms ingredients, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: prim, stiffly correct
Oscar is O in the NATO alphabet
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A recipe: fold something into good lard as it cooks in a soup.
explanation.walkthrough: Oscar joins the cooked letters of 'lard I' before they are shuffled, and PRIM goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: The primordial soup is the mixture of chemicals in which life on Earth is thought to have begun.

clue.text: Maintain this is when tennis players bounce the ball

definitions.text: this is when tennis players bounce the ball

blocks.note: first meaning: keep in its existing state

blocks.clueFragment: this is when tennis players bounce the ball
blocks.note: second meaning, read cryptically: the moment just before a player serves

explanation.surface: Keep up the ritual of bouncing the ball before you serve.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half splits the answer as PRE-SERVE: players bounce the ball just before serving.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain something is to keep it safe and unchanged over time, protecting it from decay.

clue.text: Mark possibly good spelling, ignoring half the words

indicators.note: dropping half of each word means only the front portion is kept

blocks.note: the front half of good
the front half of spelling

explanation.surface: An exam mark for good spelling that skipped half the words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a score, but it is the evangelist. Each word loses its back half.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark is one of the four New Testament books telling the life of Jesus, alongside Matthew, Luke and John.
